notes.title: Send an alarm with the same signature to the owner once
notes.source: field practice of the aos contour (factory monitoring routines, autumn 2026)
notes.body:
A monitor that runs every few minutes and finds the same problem every time
must not tell the owner about it every time. The tenth identical message is
not a signal, it is noise that teaches the owner to ignore the channel, and
the next real alarm drowns in it.

The habit that held on live nodes:

- Give each alarm a signature: the identifier of the object (a pull request
  number, a task id, a routine name) plus the kind of problem. Put the
  identifier in the text, not just the class of the problem ("PR 123 is red
  on lint", not "some PRs are red").
- Keep the signatures already sent in the routine's own state. Send again
  only when the signature changes (a new object, a different problem) or
  after an explicit snooze from the owner has expired.
- The rule for repeating lives in the routine, not in the memory of the agent
  that runs it: a fresh session does not remember what the previous one sent.

A routine that goes red a second time with the same text is a broken routine,
not a second alarm. Fix the routine (or record the snooze) instead of letting
it repeat.

notes.title: Do not promise "I will write when it is done" without a watcher
notes.source: field practice of the aos contour, agent-os#1251 (orchestration routes the promise to watch_start)
notes.body:
A chat turn ends, and nothing wakes the session up again on its own. A reply
such as "the build is running, I will tell you when it finishes" is therefore
a promise nobody keeps: the turn closes, the build finishes, and the owner
hears nothing until he asks "so how is it going?".

Before you write such a promise, hand the waiting to the node:

- start a watcher with `watch_start` on the thing you are waiting for (a CI
  run, a pull request, a command), so the node itself posts the result to the
  chat when it reaches a terminal state;
- for work that is not observable that way, set a reminder on the moment you
  expect a result, and check it then.

Only after the watcher (or the reminder) exists, say so in the reply, in the
form "watching X, the result will come here". A promise with nothing behind
it is worse than no promise: the owner waits for a message that never comes.

The same applies to a background session or a spawned worker: its report does
not wake the chat by itself unless something is set to deliver it.

notes.title: Report a state only from a command run in the same turn
notes.source: field practice of the aos contour (owner reports on rights, usage and CI, autumn 2026)
notes.body:
"The CI is green", "the node has root on this host", "we used 40% of the
week" -- each of these sounds like a fact, and each has been wrong on a live
node when it came from memory, from a document or from an earlier turn. Rights
change, usage moves every minute, a check that was green an hour ago is red on
the new head.

The habit: a claim about the current state goes into a reply only together
with a command run in this same turn that shows it.

- Rights: ask the system (for example `sudo -l`, or the node's own boundary
  file), not the canon or a note.
- Usage and limits: the node's usage tool or command, with the time of the
  reading.
- CI and pull requests: the GitHub API or `gh` on the current head sha.
- Anything else: the shortest read-only command that returns the value.

If the command cannot be run, say "not checked" and list what was tried. "I
cannot" without the list of checked options is an unchecked answer: go
through the node's tools first (the `gh` scopes, `sudo -l`, the MCP tools,
the neighbour APIs) and name what was checked.
